wiki-iran.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Iran, a country of some 90 million people whose oil exports, nuclear programme and control of one shore of the Strait of Hormuz keep it entangled with the wider world.
wiki-iran.recent: Austria revoked a visa it had already granted Mohammad Eslami, locking Iran's nuclear chief out of the IAEA General Conference in Vienna, and spokesman Abbas Goudarzi called exit from the non-proliferation treaty "readily attainable". Iranian air defences downed a US F-15E over Isfahan; its crew spent about 50 hours on the ground.

brent.standing: The world's most widely used oil benchmark, priced from North Sea crude and used to set contracts for roughly two-thirds of globally traded barrels. Refiners, airlines and importing governments price against it.
brent.recent: Drones launched from Tayeb Island in Iraq's Maysan struck the pipeline that lets Saudi Arabia ship crude from Yanbu without passing Hormuz, and traders say export stocks there run out within days. The Houthis took Yemen's Red Sea coast the same week, and a Senate bill would let Trump put 100% tariffs on buyers of Russian oil.

wti.standing: The price of a barrel of West Texas Intermediate, a light sweet crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the pricing reference for most North American oil. US petrol prices and drilling budgets follow it.
wti.recent: A US-Iran war moved from the Gulf into the price: explosions hit Iran's Kharg export island, US strikes damaged Iranian crude tankers, and Houthi fighters took Yemen's port of Mocha, contesting the Red Sea route out of Saudi Arabia. Argus counts 7 million barrels a day of lost exports; US consumer prices rose 0.4% in August on the pass-through.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas, settled at a pipeline junction in Erath, Louisiana, where major interstate lines meet. American power generation, heating and fertilizer plants price off it, and US LNG export cargoes are indexed to it.
natgas-hh.recent: Henry Hub has stayed loose while the rest of the world tightened: European October futures touched $1,004 per 1,000 cubic meters and Dutch prices passed €75 per megawatt-hour after drone strikes from Iraq's Maysan province shut Saudi Arabia's Hormuz-bypass pipeline. China and India answered the seaborne price by switching to coal and oil rather than bidding, and Bangladesh is building two LNG terminals by 2030 to lock in supply.

wheat.standing: The IMF's global wheat benchmark, a dollar-per-tonne average of export prices for the world's most widely traded food grain. It sets what flour millers pay, and bread subsidies in importing countries are budgeted against it.
wheat.recent: The UN's food agency logged a third straight monthly rise in its price index, to 133.3 points, with cereals among the drivers, and named conflict and extreme weather as the cause. Europe's drought took France's maize harvest to a four-decade low, and forecasters warned of an El Nino that could be the strongest in decades running into 2027.

rice.standing: The world price of milled rice, quoted per tonne for Thai 5% broken grade and compiled by the IMF, is the reference that importing governments budget against. It is the staple calorie for roughly half the planet, and export bans move it fast.
rice.recent: Rice blast, a fungus that destroys enough grain each year to feed tens of millions, was shown to survive the plant's defences by enzymatically switching on a catalase that neutralises the reactive-oxygen burst rice fires at it — a mechanism breeding programmes have repeatedly failed to outrun. Separately, the FAO index rose a third month, to 133.3 points.

copper.standing: The world price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal that carries electricity. Grids, motors, transformers and building wire are all claims on it, so its price is the running cost of electrification.
copper.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's reporting explains the price. What copper appeared in was biology and sabotage: Texas A&M researchers working on how immune cells use copper against bacteria in College Station, and the explosives found on power lines in Saxony, which threatened German grid hardware rather than any supply of the metal.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years. It is the reference rate the rest of the world prices against, so mortgages, corporate debt and emerging-market sovereign borrowing all reset when it moves.
us-10y.recent: Yields climbed into an expected Fed hike rather than away from one — Goldman Sachs dropped its no-hike call after Houthi forces captured Yemen's port of Mocha and oil reached $105, so the market is pricing inflation the Fed has not contained rather than just the policy rate. Norway's wealth fund weighed cutting $80bn of Treasuries into the same move.

sp500.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of 500 large US companies chosen by a committee at S&P Dow Jones Indices, and the default measure of American equity performance. Trillions in pension and index funds track it directly.
sp500.recent: Chip stocks led a global sell-off after the heads of Anthropic, OpenAI and SpaceX backed a call to slow 'reckless' AI development, with semiconductor names down 8% — a concentration that shows what investors think a pause would actually halt. Rising petrol costs pushed US inflation up in August, and bond yields reached multi-decade highs.

nasdaq100.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York. Its weighting concentrates it in a handful of very large technology firms, so a few share prices set the whole level.
nasdaq100.recent: Chip stocks led a global sell-off, falling 8% after a warning over AI spending — and the index's weighting means those names carry it. The day before, Anthropic was reported to have picked Nasdaq for an IPO that could raise $100 billion at a $2 trillion valuation, the same private-capital pile whose durability the sell-off questioned.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay at the pump, surveyed across grades and states by the Energy Information Administration. It follows crude and refining margins with a lag, and it is the most politically visible price in the country.
us-gas-retail.recent: Houthi missiles set Aramco's Red Sea refinery at Jizan ablaze while Hormuz traffic was disrupted, and Brent ran up 22% in a week — lost refining capacity and dearer crude both reaching the pump. Trump then asked Zelensky to halt strikes on Russian refineries, to keep the product squeeze from widening.

natgas-ttf.standing: The Dutch Title Transfer Facility price, the benchmark for gas delivered into northwest Europe's pipeline grid and the reference most European industrial and heating contracts settle against. Since the continent turned to seaborne LNG it clears against Asian buyers.
natgas-ttf.recent: October futures touched $1,004 per 1,000 cubic meters in Amsterdam, a level last paid in December 2022, after a rush to fill storage collided with an LNG shortage. Qatari cargoes have been held up by the Gulf war, and China and India answered the price by burning coal and oil instead — while Bangladesh committed to two new import terminals by 2030.

vix.standing: A gauge of how much volatility options traders are pricing into the S&P 500 over the next 30 days. It rises when investors pay up for downside protection, so it reads as the cost of insuring American equity risk.

fx-pkr.standing: The number of Pakistani rupees it takes to buy one US dollar. Pakistan imports nearly all of its crude and refined fuel, so the rate sets the landed cost of energy and feeds straight into domestic prices.
fx-pkr.recent: The State Bank of Pakistan held its policy rate at 11.5 per cent, citing Middle East escalation pushing oil and therefore inflation; some bankers had priced a cut. With Brent near $110 a barrel, the import bill the rupee has to cover is set in the Gulf. Islamabad raised diesel Rs6.10 to Rs409.42 a litre and answered the protests with a motorcycle fuel subsidy.

fx-ngn.standing: The exchange rate of Nigeria's currency against the US dollar, quoted as naira per dollar. Nigeria imports most of its refined fuel and much of its food, so the rate sets domestic prices, while oil sales supply almost all the dollars that defend it.
fx-ngn.recent: J.P. Morgan readmitted Nigerian federal bonds to a global index for the first time since 2015, a reclassification expected to draw $17.5 billion of passive inflows and cut yields by up to 200 basis points — dollars arriving for reasons unrelated to oil. Washington separately lifted a 12-year shipping restriction on Nigerian ports.

fx-egp.standing: The price of one US dollar in Egyptian pounds. Egypt imports most of its wheat and fuel, so this rate sets shop prices at home, and the dollars to pay for those imports come back through Suez tolls, tourism and Gulf remittances.
fx-egp.recent: Cairo's fortnight was diplomatic rather than monetary: Xi Jinping arrived for his first state visit in a decade, pitching a Middle East security framework, and Putin talked up widening Russia-Egypt trade. At home, five governorates lost their fertilizer cooperatives to a state subsidy handover. None of it accounts for the rate.

fx-try.standing: The exchange value of Turkey's currency against the US dollar. Turkish firms and the state borrow heavily in dollars while earning in lira, so every step down raises the cost of imported energy and of servicing that debt.
fx-try.recent: The lira's slide came as Ankara revised its medium-term growth forecast downward, and as the US Treasury sanctioned Golden Global Bank over Iran-related dealings, a reminder that Turkish institutions remain exposed to enforcement reaching their dollar access. Erdogan meanwhile pressed Turkey's SCO membership bid while denying any abandonment of the West.

fx-bdt.standing: The price of one US dollar in Bangladeshi taka, the managed rate Bangladesh Bank steers within a narrow band. The country imports its fuel, industrial inputs and much of its food, so the rate sets the cost of nearly everything that lands at Chittagong.
fx-bdt.recent: Dhaka spent the month committing to more dollar-denominated energy imports rather than fewer: two new LNG terminals due by 2030, and a $1 billion Islamic Development Bank facility for domestic refining capacity that only pays off years out. A ministerial row with Delhi over the terms of the relationship added friction to the trade Bangladesh runs closest to home.

fx-idr.standing: Indonesia's currency, quoted as rupiah per US dollar, so a rising number means a weaker rupiah. Southeast Asia's largest economy prices its commodity exports and services its foreign borrowing against this rate.
fx-idr.recent: The fortnight's news from Jakarta was disaster and energy policy rather than macro: Anak Krakatau's ash closed Soekarno-Hatta, a ferry went down in the Java Sea, peat fires pushed Malaysia to declare a haze emergency, and parliament ratified a deal opening 138 oil and gas blocks to Russia. None of that accounts for the rate.

fx-lbp.standing: The street and official exchange rate of Lebanon's currency against the US dollar. Since the 2019 banking collapse it has been held near a fixed peg by the central bank, and almost all pricing inside Lebanon is done in dollars anyway.
fx-lbp.recent: The rate barely moved while the south burned: Israeli forces destroyed Ghandour Hospital in Nabatieh on 6 September, killing seven, and detonated a Hezbollah tunnel network under Ali al-Taher on 11 September with force the US Geological Survey logged as a 4.1 tremor. Lebanese officials said talks with Israel were unlikely the following week.

fx-cny.standing: The number of yuan it takes to buy one US dollar, so a falling line is a strengthening currency. The People's Bank of China fixes a daily midpoint and permits trading only in a band around it, making the level partly a policy decision.
fx-cny.recent: The fortnight's China news does not bear on the exchange rate: Xi pitching an AI "open ecosystem" to BRICS in New Delhi, robot prices in Hangzhou falling to $4,000, solar capacity overtaking coal, and seven-year sentences for Hong Kong vigil organisers. None of it accounts for the rate.

fx-inr.standing: The rupee's price against the US dollar, quoted as rupees per dollar, so a higher number means a weaker rupee. India buys most of its crude and much of its electronics abroad, so the rate passes into domestic prices and into the dollar value of everything the economy produces.
fx-inr.recent: Washington's Senate passed a bill letting Trump impose 100% tariffs on buyers of Russian oil, aimed squarely at India's discounted crude purchases. The currency is also why India slipped to sixth-largest economy despite 7.8% growth: the ranking is measured in dollars, and a rebasing that cut last year's economic base by 7% compounded it. New Delhi's answer at the BRICS summit was to push settlement in local currencies.

fx-brl.standing: The value of Brazil's real against the US dollar, quoted as reais per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker real. Brazil is a major exporter of soy, iron ore and crude, and the rate sets the local value of those earnings.
fx-brl.recent: Brazilian politics dominated the fortnight: federal police opened a corruption probe into Flávio Bolsonaro over public funds routed through film financing, and a poll showed the socialist president's lead evaporating with the election tightening. Washington separately designated the PCC, Brazil's largest gang, a terrorist organisation.

fx-mxn.standing: Pesos per US dollar — the rate at which Mexico's currency trades against that of its largest trading partner. Remittances, cross-border manufacturing and dollar-priced commodity exports all settle through it.
fx-mxn.recent: The fortnight's reporting on Mexico ran to the 1944 water treaty and the delivery shortfall pressing on farmers, and to a solar subsidy cutting household power bills in Mexicali. Neither touches the currency, and nothing in the window accounts for the peso's move.

fx-eur.standing: The exchange rate between the euro — the shared currency of 20 European Union member states — and the US dollar. It is the most heavily traded currency pair in the world, and it prices the euro area's imports and dollar debts.
fx-eur.recent: The fortnight's European news was political rather than monetary: the AfD's landslide in Saxony-Anhalt, the collapse of the Future Combat Air System between France and Germany, and Finland moving under French nuclear cover. None of it accounts for the rate.

fx-jpy.standing: The exchange rate between Japan's currency and the US dollar, quoted as yen per dollar, so a higher number means a weaker yen. It is the world's most traded currency pair after the euro, and the funding leg of carry trades that reach far beyond Japan.
fx-jpy.recent: Treasury Secretary Bessent pressed the Bank of Japan to raise rates, an unusual public intervention in another country's monetary policy, and Tokyo began weighing whether pension money could be steered to defend the currency instead. The yen then surged as the dollar fell on Waller's comments.

fx-rub.standing: The exchange rate of Russia's currency against the US dollar, quoted as rubles per dollar. Capital controls and oil revenue set its floor, and it is the cleanest daily read on how much sanctions pressure is actually reaching Moscow's finances.
fx-rub.recent: A Senate-passed bill would let Trump impose 100% tariffs on buyers of Russian oil, aimed squarely at India — whose purchases underwrite the export earnings the currency rests on. European states have been detaining aging tankers from the shadow fleet that carries those barrels, drawing a warning from Putin, while Washington asked Kyiv to stop striking Russian refineries.

fx-zar.standing: The price of one US dollar in South African rand. The rand is among the most heavily traded currencies in the emerging world and clears freely around the clock, so it moves on global risk appetite as readily as on domestic news.
fx-zar.recent: The fortnight's South African news ran to domestic politics rather than the economy: Helen Zille campaigning in Soweto ahead of the 4 November local elections, and Nigeria's Assembly suspending all visits to South Africa. Neither reaches the exchange rate.

btc.standing: The dollar price of one bitcoin, the first and largest cryptocurrency, quoted continuously on exchanges worldwide. It has no issuer and no cash flow, so it trades on liquidity conditions and on what regulators decide it legally is.
btc.recent: Washington is writing the rules rather than litigating them: the House Ways and Means Committee put out a 114-page bill that would fix crypto's place in the tax code, with a de minimis exemption that decides whether a token can be spent at all, and the Senate set a cloture vote on the CLARITY Act. Access widened too, after the Commodity Futures Trading Commission cleared US traders into offshore perpetuals.

eth.standing: The native token of Ethereum, the programmable blockchain most stablecoins and tokenised assets are issued on. Fees for every transaction and contract on that network are paid in it, so demand for the token tracks use of the chain.
eth.recent: US rulemaking moved from enforcement to statute on several fronts at once: the House Ways and Means Committee released a 114-page bill writing crypto into the tax code, with a de minimis exemption that decides whether tokens can be spent without a taxable disposal, the Senate set a cloture vote on the CLARITY Act, and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission cleared US access to crypto perpetuals in Singapore.

paxg.standing: A token redeemable for one fine troy ounce of London Good Delivery bullion held in vaults, so it trades at the spot gold price rather than at a crypto valuation. It is how holders of gold take a position without arranging storage.
paxg.recent: A US payroll surge revived bets on a September rate hike, and higher oil kept those bets alive — both raise the return on holding cash against metal that pays nothing. Underneath, custody is moving: the Dutch central bank shifted $11.6bn out of New York for London, and the US Treasury sanctioned Turkey's Golden Global Bank over Iran-linked flows.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: The Wikipedia article on artificial intelligence, and the daily count of people who open it. It is a proxy for how far the subject has travelled beyond the industry that builds it, rather than a measure of anything the technology does.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Anthropic's Amodei warned that an AI "swarm" could seize the internet as AI firms called for a slowdown, and chip stocks fell 8% while SoftBank shed 13% in Tokyo. Trump called the safety warnings a "sick conspiracy" and declined guardrails; OpenAI shelved IPO paperwork it was weeks from filing.

wiki-russia.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Russia, the world's largest country by land area and a permanent member of the UN Security Council. It rises when a war, a sanctions decision or a summit sends people to look up the basics.
wiki-russia.recent: Russia launched 863 drones at Ukraine in a single night, hitting close to the Polish border, and struck Odesa in an attack that killed four and wounded 37. Putin called European troops in Ukraine grounds for "war" and warned Europe over its detentions of aging tankers, while a US Senate bill moved to let Trump put 100% tariffs on buyers of Russian oil.

wiki-pakistan.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Pakistan, a country of roughly 240 million people. Traffic to a country's encyclopedia entry rises when something there reaches an audience with no prior reason to look it up.
wiki-pakistan.recent: Fuel dominated the fortnight: a petroleum levy of 114 rupees a litre drew a march in Gujranwala, diesel then rose Rs6.10 to Rs409.42, and Shehbaz Sharif answered with a subsidy narrowed to motorcycles. Islamabad also stepped between Iran and Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks put the Makkah defence pact in play.

wiki-china.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on China. It rises when the country's politics, technology or diplomacy reach a wide audience, so it tracks how many people abroad are looking the place up rather than anything happening inside it.
wiki-china.recent: Hangzhou firms pushed a walking humanoid to $13,500 and a capable robot dog to $4,000, undercutting Western makers on price rather than capability. Chipmaker Enflame tripled on its Shanghai debut to $27.6 billion on the strength of export controls that shut rivals out, and Xi used Modi's BRICS summit to pitch an AI "open ecosystem" to the bloc.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The 33-kilometre-wide channel between Iran and Oman linking the Gulf to the Arabian Sea, and the only sea route out for Gulf crude and LNG. Roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes it, with no pipeline able to replace more than a fraction.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: The mid-August peak came as US strikes on Iran resumed and Brent pushed past $100; Washington then struck Iranian tankers off Kharg and Jask, and Iran's Rezaei threatened a Gulf exclusion zone and floated transit fees. A projectile killed one sailor off Qeshm Island, and Bahrain's empty chair collapsed the Muscat talks.

wiki-india.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on India, a country of some 1.4 billion people. The count climbs when Delhi hosts something the rest of the world has to look up.
wiki-india.recent: Modi hosted the BRICS summit in New Delhi, fitting 15 bilateral meetings into three days while Xi and Putin shared the stage and Iran pressed for easier membership of the bloc's New Development Bank. India used the week to sell its own plumbing abroad — the UPI instant-payment network that clears over 250 billion transfers a year, and its examination platform.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: A projectile killed a sailor on a tanker off Qeshm Island, and Iran is weighing fees on transits while Gulf states shelved talks in Muscat over the channel. The usual hedge failed alongside it: drones from Iraq's Maysan province shut Saudi Arabia's East-West bypass pipeline, leaving Yanbu export stocks days from empty.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Houthi fighters took the coffee port of Mokha, 75 kilometres up the coast, then Perim Island inside the shipping lane itself, giving one party to the war physical control of both banks. Some 46,000 people fled the Red Sea coast as the front moved, and Brent reached $109.50 a barrel on Sept. 9.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Traffic tracks the southern end of the route rather than the canal itself. Houthi fighters seized Yemen's Red Sea coast and the port of Mocha, then took Perim Island beside Bab al-Mandab, the gate every northbound Suez transit must pass; 46,000 people fled the coast, and Brent went above $108.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: The US-Iran war has kept Qatari LNG from moving through Hormuz; China and India cut imports to multi-year lows and burned coal and oil instead, so cargoes that would have run east through this strait never loaded. Iran's Strait Authority has meanwhile expanded its non-compliant vessel list, pushing insurers off tanker cover.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Transit capacity is being rationed again as El Niño builds: the Panama Canal Authority is moving daily slots from 32 toward 29, and the UN puts the odds the event persists into February near 100%, with Pacific temperatures already up more than 2C in six months. Forecasters expect a record Amazon drought on the same pattern.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Transits thinned after a Turkish cargo ship sank off Silivri following a collision in the Marmara approach on 2 September, leaving ten crew missing and pushing traffic into the queue outside the strait. Grain leaving through it matters more than usual: the UN food index has now climbed three straight months, to 133.3 points.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: The fortnight's news from both shores was about people and sanctions rather than hulls: more than 72,000 crossed into Ceuta in July and Morocco deported over 4,000 from Tangier, while a Senate bill would tariff buyers of Russian oil and two tankers were attacked leaving Hormuz. None of it accounts for what these vessels are doing.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Masked protesters shut Britain's busiest ferry port at Dover on 5 September, halting cross-Channel freight, and two days later crowds at Portsmouth blocked buses carrying 140 asylum seekers who had crossed from Normandy. The disruption was at the quayside rather than in the water, so the lane itself kept working.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: The Gulf crisis that would normally push ships onto this route arrived as disruption at the loading end instead: US strikes on Iranian crude tankers, explosions on Kharg, and three tankers turning back at Hormuz with no shots fired. Iran's Strait Authority has also moved against insurers, and cargo that never loads never needs a detour.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's coverage of the war accounts for traffic stopping here: the reporting tracks drones — 863 launched at Ukraine in one night — strikes on Odesa that wounded 37, and a drone hitting a Warsaw-bound train two kilometres from Poland, all of it far to the west. The one maritime thread is European states detaining aging Russian tankers, which Putin has warned over, and that is a Baltic and North Sea story rather than an Azov one.

mkt:tadawul.standing: Saudi Arabia's main stock index, tracking the companies listed on the Saudi Exchange in Riyadh. It is the Arab world's largest market by value, dominated by Aramco, and it trades Sunday to Thursday, opening the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: Drones launched from Iraq's Maysan province shut the East-West pipeline that lets Saudi crude bypass Hormuz, and traders at Yanbu said export stocks would run out within days. Houthi forces took Mocha and the Red Sea coast the same week, closing the third route out, and fired missiles and drones at King Khalid Air Base.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so the index level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: Ankara revised its medium-term growth forecast downward, writing the regional war into the official numbers that Turkish earnings are set against. The US Treasury sanctioned Golden Global Bank over Iran-linked dealings, a reminder that Turkish financial institutions remain exposed to enforcement from Washington even as Erdogan pushes an SCO membership bid he insists is not a turn away from NATO.

mkt:dfm.standing: The benchmark index of the Dubai Financial Market, the United Arab Emirates's largest listed venue, weighted toward property developers and banks. It trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh's Sunday-start week.
mkt:dfm.recent: Dubai's listed property and banking names sit inside a war economy: US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers, the closure of Hormuz pushed Emirates–Oman land trade up 175%, and hotel demand fell to 7% of normal levels. Algeria then expelled the UAE's envoy, and Abu Dhabi opened talks with Tehran at the BRICS summit.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The 30 largest companies listed on Bursa Malaysia in Kuala Lumpur, weighted by free-float market value. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.

mkt:idx.standing: The benchmark index of the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, tracking every listed company on the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country. Commodity producers and banks dominate it.
mkt:idx.recent: The quarter's run has been built on resource extraction that keeps generating disasters: 138 oil and gas blocks were opened to Russia under a bloc deal parliament had already ratified, while the nickel boom that anchors the export story is powered by private captive coal plants. Peat fires emitted 76 million tonnes of carbon and closed schools across the Malaysian border.

mkt:tse.standing: The 225 large Japanese companies tracked by a price-weighted average on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Asia's largest market and the first major one to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: SoftBank shares slumped 13% on Monday as markets repriced how fast AI spending will actually arrive, dragging the index's heaviest constituents with it. The yen has been the other pressure: US Treasury Secretary Bessent urged Japan to raise rates, and Tokyo has weighed steering the currency through pension money rather than intervention.

mkt:hkex.standing: Hong Kong's benchmark index, tracking the largest companies listed on the Hong Kong exchange — mostly mainland Chinese firms. It is where Chinese corporate earnings meet foreign money that can leave freely, so it prices China risk faster than any onshore market.
mkt:hkex.recent: Enflame's Shanghai debut tripled on its first day to a $27.6 billion valuation, a chipmaker priced by what US export controls keep out rather than by what it ships. Hangzhou's robot makers cut a walking humanoid to $13,500 and a quadruped to $4,000, undercutting Western rivals by an order of magnitude.

mkt:sse.standing: Mainland China's main board, in Shanghai, tracking every A- and B-share listed there. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The board's technology names carry the story: Enflame tripled on debut in Shanghai to $27.6 billion, a valuation written by the export controls that handed it a captive domestic market for AI chips. The same cost curve runs through hardware — a Hangzhou walking robot at $13,500 and a capable robot dog at $4,000 — while Xi used the BRICS summit in New Delhi to pitch an AI "open ecosystem" outside Washington's reach.

mkt:krx.standing: The main index of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, tracking every common stock listed on its senior board. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix dominate it, which makes it a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.

mkt:bse.standing: The 30-company benchmark of the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, Asia's oldest exchange, founded in 1875, and the standard reading of Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: A Senate-passed bill lets Trump tariff buyers of Russian oil at 100%, and India is the target — the cost lands on the refiners and lenders the index is built from. Gulf hostilities have already cut Indian LNG imports to multi-year lows, pushing power generation and industry back onto coal.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies listed on the Singapore Exchange, and the benchmark for Southeast Asia's financial hub. Banks and regional property groups carry most of its weight.
mkt:sgx.recent: Singapore spent the window widening what its exchange clears: SGX bitcoin and ether perpetual futures opened to US institutions after the Commodity Futures Trading Commission cleared access, and Circle paid $400 million for Tazapay's payment licenses in more than 100 markets. China's August exports rose 25% to $401 billion, steadying the regional trade flows the index's banks lend against.

mkt:twse.standing: The capitalisation-weighted index of all common shares listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: Nvidia paid $3.5 billion for convertible bonds giving it an option on MediaTek, whose shares jumped 10% and pulled the index's chip weighting with them. Taipei also charged Beijing with running undeclared chip labs to poach Taiwanese engineers, and with espionage on the Pacific forum floor.

mkt:set.standing: The main board index of the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, weighted by market value across the listed companies on it. Banks, energy and tourism-exposed firms carry it, so it moves with visitor numbers and fuel costs.
mkt:set.recent: Thai artillery hit the Preah Vihear temple complex on the Cambodian border, and UNESCO has now documented the damage while Bangkok answers that Cambodia stationed troops there first — a live border war on the frontier of a market that depends on visitors. Bangkok's semiconductor plan also runs through Washington, which licenses the fabrication equipment.

mkt:pse.standing: The Philippine Stock Exchange Index, the 30 largest and most actively traded companies listed in Manila. It is a small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: Manila's political class spent the fortnight in court: an anti-graft court ordered the arrest of Marcos's cousin Romualdez over flood-control kickbacks, and Vice President Sara Duterte posted bail on charges of threatening the president. Neither the construction procurement scandal nor the succession fight has a clean read for domestic earnings.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by float-adjusted market value. Miners and the big four banks dominate it, so it often turns on Chinese demand data before other markets open.
mkt:asx.recent: The drag through the window came from the index's two heaviest sectors at once: miners and energy stocks led the falls, and a threatened round of US tariffs knocked the market again. Domestically, home prices fell for a fifth straight month and buyer numbers collapsed against a rate wall the banks cannot lend around.

mkt:jse.standing: The FTSE/JSE All Share tracks nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in South Africa, weighted by market value. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the continent's only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: South Africa's economy contracted over a quarter as oil prices fed through, and the domestic picture has been one of strained public services — Gauteng's nurses gave the province a one-month ultimatum over austerity in the health system. Relations with Nigeria also soured: Abuja's lawmakers suspended all official visits after xenophobic attacks, and Ondo State began resettling nearly 3,000 returnees.

mkt:b3.standing: The benchmark index of B3 in São Paulo, tracking the most heavily traded shares on Brazil's only stock exchange. Iron ore and oil producers weigh heavily in it, and domestic interest rates set what those earnings are worth.
mkt:b3.recent: A corruption investigation reached Flávio Bolsonaro over public film financing as the election tightened, while Washington's designation of the PCC, Brazil's largest gang, as a terror organisation handed the campaign a security fight with extraterritorial legal reach. The Banco Master scandal widened into politics over the same days.

mkt:bmv.standing: The main index of the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City, tracking a selection of the most liquid and heavily weighted companies listed there. Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: Water sits at the centre of the economic friction with the United States: Mexico has fallen behind on the deliveries the 1944 treaty obliges it to make, and the shortfall lands on farmers in the north whose output and credit feed the listed agro and banking names. Washington's posture toward Mexico has hardened alongside it.

mkt:byma.standing: The benchmark index of the Buenos Aires exchange, tracking Argentina's most heavily traded listed companies. Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years — direction over a day means something; the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: Milei reopened the Falklands claim, sanctioning 45 firms tied to UK-linked oil drilling around the islands, and Trump put the long-standing US position on the dispute under review. Washington then approved a $103m Black Hawk sale to Buenos Aires. Monthly inflation, meanwhile, fell to a 14-month low.

mkt:tsx.standing: Canada's benchmark index, tracking the largest companies listed in Toronto by float-adjusted market value. Oil and gas producers, miners and the big domestic banks dominate the weighting, so it trades as much on commodities as on Canadian growth.
mkt:tsx.recent: Washington put 50% tariffs on Canadian goods and banned dairy, alcohol and motorcycles outright, then threatened Bombardier by name; Ottawa's $20 billion in counter-tariffs took effect Tuesday. Carney answered by pitching associate EU membership to investors managing $72tn in Toronto — a reorientation of trade built to run north-south.

mkt:nyse.standing: The 500 leading US-listed companies, weighted by market value and chosen by a selection committee, spanning the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: US business news in the window was sector-specific rather than market-wide: Apple launched a $1,999 foldable phone, the EPA moved to let coal plants stop capturing their emissions, and the Senate set a cloture vote on crypto market structure while the House wrote crypto into tax law. None of it accounts for the index as a whole.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies by value on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market. Most FTSE 100 revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: London's weight in the index is financial rather than industrial: the Financial Conduct Authority put the city's share of world gold trading at 70% while consulting on tokenised bullion, and the question of whether a token is allocated metal or a claim on a bank decides who carries the risk. Nothing in the fortnight's politics — Swinney's 2031 referendum target, Trump's backing for Irish unification — reaches the index.

mkt:xetra.standing: The 40 largest listed companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. Its weight in carmakers, chemicals and industrial machinery makes it Europe's clearest read on export demand.
mkt:xetra.recent: Saxony-Anhalt handed the AfD nearly 44% and the first far-right state win since the war, with about 150,000 people marching across 20 German cities afterwards; the other parties held the firewall, leaving coalition arithmetic unresolved. Deutsche Bank raised its ECB peak call to 2.75% on energy costs feeding second-round inflation.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest listed companies on Euronext Paris, France's main market. Luxury goods and energy dominate it, making the index unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The blue-chip index of the 25 most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the descendant of the world's oldest stock exchange. A single chip-equipment maker, ASML, carries enough weight to move the whole index on its own.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: Amsterdam is where Europe prices its gas, and the TTF contract traded there ran to a three-year high above €75 per megawatt-hour before October futures reached $1,004 per 1,000 cubic meters — an energy cost that lands on the industrial names listed in the same city. The Dutch central bank also moved $11.6bn in gold out of New York to London.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Madrid exchange, Spain's main market. Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make it a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Domestic politics ran hot without reaching the tape: parliament voted 168 to 31 to open citizenship to Sahrawis, and more than 72,000 crossings into Ceuta in July brought protests and a public challenge to Morocco's border control. None of that explains the index, and nothing else in the fortnight's reporting accounts for the move.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 most heavily traded companies on the Milan exchange, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities dominate it, which makes it the European index most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: Milan's drift came without a domestic shock: Giorgia Meloni passed 1,413 days in office, the longest any Italian government has lasted, and the stability that once carried a risk premium is now priced in. The pressure was external — a global bond slump that lifted yields, and a state plane flying Gen. Osama Almasri Njeem back to Tripoli, testing Rome's border deal rather than its balance sheet.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index, the 20 largest and most traded companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The 30 most traded companies on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main market. Nordic industrials and telecoms dominate it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: Sweden voted on 13 September in a race close enough that SVT's exit poll gave the opposition 51.3% and the count left the blocs at 176 seats to 173 with 95% in. The Sweden Democrats' entry into government was on the ballot for the first time, and neither side can form a majority without a partner it has spent the campaign ruling out.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only public equity market. Trades Sunday to Thursday, and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at the upcoming meeting. Traders buy and sell the outcome, so the price is the going rate for a bet on the Fed sitting still.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: The bet on the Fed holding steady got cheaper as the case for a hike hardened: Houthi fighters took Yemen's port of Mocha on 10 September, oil ran to $105, and Goldman Sachs dropped its no-hike call on 13 September. A payroll surge and a 10-year Treasury yield at 5% left little room for the Fed to wait.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia biography of the 45th and 47th President of the United States. The count rises with whatever he has just done, which makes it a rough register of how far a given American political event travelled.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: The early-September peak came as US forces struck new targets in Iran and Tehran warned of a "crushing blow"; eleven people were killed in those strikes. Trump has since tied the war's end to the midterms, warned Zelenskyy off Russian diesel refineries as US diesel topped $6.06 a gallon, and backed a united Ireland from Doonbeg.

wiki-united-states.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on the United States. It is one of the most-read country pages on the site, so its baseline is high and only large events lift it above the ordinary churn of school terms and holidays.
wiki-united-states.recent: US strikes on Iran resumed in early September, with 11 killed and Tehran warning of a 'more painful response' to further attacks; an American jet was later downed by Iranian air defence over Isfahan. At home, the Supreme Court left a mail-ballot injunction standing and a judge blocked the Homeland Security four-year student visa cap.

fed-funds.standing: The overnight interest rate the Federal Reserve sets for lending between US banks. It is the base cost of dollars, so it feeds into every loan priced off the dollar, at home and in the much larger market for dollar credit outside the United States.
fed-funds.recent: Policy has been easing, but the war changed the argument: Houthi fighters captured Yemen's port of Mocha, oil ran to $105, and August consumer prices rose 0.4% with the energy bill inside them. A payroll surge followed, Goldman Sachs dropped its no-hike call, and the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5%.

ecb-rate.standing: The rate the European Central Bank pays on overnight deposits banks park with it, and the floor under every euro-denominated borrowing cost. Where it sits sets mortgage, business-loan and government funding rates across the twenty-euro-area economies.
ecb-rate.recent: The cutting cycle has stalled on energy: with Brent near $110 a barrel after the Saudi pipeline outage, Frankfurt is weighing second-round effects rather than further easing, and Deutsche Bank has moved its expected peak to 2.75% — a tightening path, not a loosening one. The same shock is being answered elsewhere with holds, as in Karachi.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force looking for work and unable to find it, published monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The Federal Reserve weighs it against inflation when setting rates, so markets move on each release.
us-unemployment.recent: The jobs report published on 5 September was solid enough that yields and the dollar rose on it while stocks eased — the reaction of a market reading a labour market too firm to force the Fed's hand. Nothing else in the fortnight's reporting points to a deterioration in hiring.

xag.standing: The spot price of a troy ounce of silver, quoted here through a metal-backed token that settles against vaulted bullion. Silver is both a monetary metal and an industrial input, so it answers to investors and to factories at the same time.
xag.recent: Nothing in the window accounts for the move. What it carries instead is demand: China's installed solar capacity passed coal, Gulf panel imports fell as war disrupted supply chains, and Pakistan moved to mandate batteries in its next 800MW solar and wind auction — solar cells are silver's largest industrial use.

wiki-petroleum.standing: Crude oil and the refined fuels drawn from it — the feedstock behind petrol, diesel, jet fuel, plastics and fertiliser. Its price sets transport and manufacturing costs worldwide, and governments subsidise or tax it to control what households pay.
wiki-petroleum.recent: A US-Iran war reached the oil trade from two directions at once. Houthi forces took Yemen's Red Sea coast and the port of Mocha, and drones flown from Iraq struck the Saudi pipeline built to bypass Hormuz, cutting Yanbu's export stocks to days. US pump prices passed $4.03 a gallon; Pakistan answered its 114-rupee levy with a motorcycle fuel subsidy.

us-cpi.standing: The year-over-year change in the US consumer price index, compiled monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics from a basket of household goods, rents and services. It sets the terms of Federal Reserve policy and reprices bonds, wages and benefits worldwide.
us-cpi.recent: August consumer prices rose 0.4% on the month, a reading Washington traced to the war's reach into the index rather than to domestic demand.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A count of laden tanker departures through the Strait of Hormuz, the sea lane between Iran and Oman that carries roughly a fifth of the world's oil. Nothing leaves the Gulf's export terminals without passing through it.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: The US struck Iranian tankers at Kharg and Jask on Tuesday, Iran answered with missiles at bases in Jordan and Bahrain, and a projectile killed one sailor off Qeshm Island. Tehran's Strait Authority then added vessels to a non-compliant list and floated transit fees; Emirates-Oman land trade jumped 175% as cargo went around.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: The count of container ships passing daily through the strait between Yemen and Djibouti, the southern gate of the Red Sea and the only sea route from Asia to the Suez Canal. Traffic here decides whether Europe-Asia cargo sails via Egypt or around Africa.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: Houthi fighters took Mokha, then the rest of Yemen's Red Sea coast, and now hold Perim Island inside the shipping lane itself; 46,000 people fled the coast in a week. Saudi jets answered with dozens of sorties a day from Khamis Mushait, and Brent passed $108 as the lane's owners changed.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of cargo ships passing through Egypt's Suez Canal each day, the sea route between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea. Roughly a tenth of world seaborne trade uses it, and every diverted vessel adds around two weeks around Africa.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: Houthi fighters took the Red Sea coast, seizing Mocha and then Perim Island in the Bab al-Mandab strait — the southern gate every Suez-bound ship must pass. Missiles set an Aramco refinery ablaze at Jizan and struck King Khalid Air Base, and the US hit Iranian tankers off Kharg and Jask.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: The number of ships passing through the Panama Canal each day, the lock-and-lake shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. The locks run on rainwater held in Gatún Lake, so a dry year rations the sailings container and grain lines depend on.
portwatch-panama-total.recent: The canal authority is weighing further cuts to daily slots as El Niño draws down the lake that feeds the locks, with its new chief signalling a drop toward 29. The UN puts the odds the event persists into February near 100% and forecasters expect it to run well into 2027, so the rationing is being set against a dry season that has not yet arrived.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The count of vessels passing each day through the Strait of Malacca between Malaysia, Indonesia and Singapore, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to East Asia. Most of China's and Japan's imported oil rides through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: The strait carries the crude that Hormuz cannot: a projectile killed a sailor off Qeshm Island, US strikes hit three Iranian tankers, Tehran began weighing tolls on Hormuz transit, and Brent topped $100. Houthi control of Yemen's Red Sea coast closed the other alternative, leaving Malacca the route east.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: A daily count of the ships passing through the channel between Taiwan and mainland China — the direct route from Northeast Asian ports to everywhere south and west of them, and a waterway both navies use to make a point.
portwatch-taiwan-total.recent: The fortnight's shipping news sat elsewhere: the Houthis took Yemen's Red Sea coast, a projectile killed one sailor off Qeshm Island and shelved the Muscat talks on Hormuz, and China and India cut LNG buying to burn coal instead. None of it reaches the Taiwan Strait.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The daily count of vessels passing through the Strait of Dover, the narrow sea lane between England and France that funnels most traffic between the North Sea and the Atlantic past two of Europe's busiest ferry ports.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The count of merchant vessels passing daily through the nine-mile channel between Spain and Morocco that links the Atlantic to the Mediterranean. Every Suez-bound cargo from the Americas and West Africa funnels through it.
portwatch-gibraltar-total.recent: Traffic through the strait is being reshaped by the war further east: Houthi forces took control of the Bab al-Mandab after seizing Yemen's port of Mocha, and a projectile killed a sailor off Qeshm Island in Hormuz, pushing Brent above $100 and sending Asia-Europe cargoes around the Cape and back in past Gibraltar.

poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if United Russia — the party backing Vladimir Putin that has held a parliamentary majority since the 2000s — takes the most seats. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome.
poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.recent: The fortnight's Russian news ran to the war and its edges: Putin calling European troops in Ukraine a "war", and a treason case in Moscow against an embassy guard that rests on a confession and nothing else. None of it bears on how many seats the party takes.

wiki-israel.standing: The English Wikipedia article on Israel, and the daily count of people who open it. Readership of a country page tracks who is looking the country up rather than who follows it, so it rises with people arriving from outside the subject.
wiki-israel.recent: Britain's position hardened through the window: twelve countries including France and the UK moved to sanction trade from Israeli settlements, Israel shut the British consulate in Jerusalem that served Palestinians, and 300 British soldiers turned out to have trained under Elbit Systems. Haaretz then reported a UAE warning to Netanyahu before 7 October, which he threatened to sue over.

poly-will-david-lisnard-win-the-2027-fre.standing: A Polymarket contract on David Lisnard — mayor of Cannes and head of France's association of mayors — winning the 2027 presidential election. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, quoted out of 100.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether American forces mount a ground invasion of Iran before 2027. It prices a war that would shut the Gulf's oil exports, so it moves alongside crude and freight rather than ahead of them.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: Traders held the bet steady through a fortnight in which the fighting stayed aerial and deniable: Iranian air defences destroyed a US F-15E Strike Eagle over Isfahan and its crew spent roughly 50 hours on the ground before recovery, while Washington denied Mohammad Eslami and his delegation visas for the IAEA conference in Vienna and Tehran called treaty exit "readily attainable.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: Daily readership of the Wikipedia article on the Houthis, the Zaydi Shia armed movement that governs much of northern Yemen. Traffic on it rises when the group's fighting reaches shipping lanes or its neighbours' territory.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: Houthi fighters took Mokha on Sept. 10 and then Perim Island, putting them astride the Bab al-Mandab shipping lane, and 46,000 people fled the Red Sea coast in a week. Missiles hit four Saudi cities on Sept. 8 and King Khalid Air Base at Khamis Mushait, with Yahya Saree claiming the sorties.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Washington lifts its naval blockade of Iranian ports before the end of September 2026. It is a bet on the war's off-ramp, and the price tracks how much traders believe the campaign is near a negotiated stop.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Traders priced an early exit out as the war widened rather than wound down. Gulf mediation collapsed — Muscat's Hormuz talks were shelved after a projectile killed a sailor off Qeshm Island, with Bahrain boycotting outright — while Washington denied Mohammad Eslami a visa for the IAEA conference in Vienna and Tehran called treaty exit "readily attainable.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: Pageviews for the English Wikipedia article on Saudi Arabia, the Gulf kingdom that holds Islam's two holiest cities and the world's largest spare crude capacity. Readership climbs when the country is at war or its oil exports are interrupted.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: Houthi forces seized Mocha and the Red Sea coast, then fired missiles and drones at King Khalid Air Base at Khamis Mushait, the field the Saudi sorties over Yemen fly from. Separate drones launched from Maysan province in Iraq shut the East-West pipeline built to bypass Hormuz, and Yanbu export stocks were days from running dry.

poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the United States enacts the Clarity Act, the bill that would divide oversight of digital assets between the securities and commodities regulators. Traders price the odds of a signature before the year ends.
poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.recent: New Jersey has asked the Supreme Court to decide whether prediction markets trade swaps or run gambling, a question that would settle which agency writes the rules the bill assumes; a UK regulator is separately weighing an end to its own ban on financial prediction markets. Neither resolves the legislative calendar.

wiki-yemen.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Yemen, the country at the southern end of the Arabian Peninsula whose coast forms one side of the Bab al-Mandab Strait. Traffic to it tracks how widely a war there is being followed.
wiki-yemen.recent: The Houthis seized Mokha, the coffee port 75 kilometers from Bab al-Mandab, taking the Red Sea coast and the approach to the strait most of the world's shipping uses. It followed strikes on Saudi energy facilities that wounded 73 and halted production, and Saudi jets answered with 54 sorties over five provinces in a day. Some 46,000 people fled the coast.

poly-israel-closes-its-airspace-by-septe.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Israel shuts its civil airspace to commercial traffic before a set date. It settles on the aviation authority's own closure notice, so it prices how close traders think the country is to a missile exchange that would ground flights.
poly-israel-closes-its-airspace-by-septe.recent: The bet was cheap until strikes widened past Gaza: Israeli artillery hit Zawtar al-Sharqiyah in Nabatieh, a demolition of Hezbollah tunnels registered as a 4.1 tremor with the US Geological Survey, and US forces struck Iranian tankers while Houthis hit Saudi oil facilities and took Yemen's port of Mocha.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-d-senate-d-ho.standing: A Polymarket contract on the 2026 US midterms paying out only if Democrats win control of both the Senate and the House. Traders price the joint outcome, so it sits below the odds of either chamber flipping on its own.

poly-fed-rate-hike-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve raises its policy rate at any point during 2026. Traders buy and sell the outcome, so the price is a live wager on tightening rather than an official projection.
poly-fed-rate-hike-in-2026.recent: A war premium reached policy: Houthi forces took Yemen's port of Mocha, oil ran to $105, and a September payroll surge landed on top of it. Goldman Sachs dropped its no-hike call, and the 10-year Treasury yield touched 5% with bettors treating a Washington hike as close to settled.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency whose ledger hides sender, receiver and amount by default, using ring signatures and stealth addresses. That opacity is why exchanges in several jurisdictions have delisted it and why it is the preferred settlement asset for extortion payments.
xmr.recent: A group calling itself VantaCore has hit at least seven Russian companies with custom ransomware, the kind of campaign that settles in an asset where the payment trail cannot be followed. Nothing else in the fortnight's reporting accounts for the size of the move.

poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Flávio Bolsonaro takes Brazil's presidency in the 2026 election. Traders price it in cents on the dollar, so the number is the market's cost of betting on a Bolsonaro restoration, not a poll.
poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.recent: Brazilian prosecutors opened a corruption investigation into Flávio Bolsonaro on 11 September, and the contract has been repricing around a race that tightened rather than around the probe. The wider run of far-right results — the AfD's win in Saxony-Anhalt and the Sweden Democrats' weight in a knife-edge Riksdag — has been read across to Brazil, though none of it touches the Brazilian ballot.

poly-will-josh-shapiro-win-the-2028-demo.standing: A Polymarket contract that settles at 100 if Josh Shapiro, the Democratic governor of Pennsylvania, becomes his party's presidential nominee in 2028. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in a field with no incumbent.
poly-will-josh-shapiro-win-the-2028-demo.recent: Nothing in the fortnight touches Shapiro or the nomination field. What the period did carry was about the venue rather than the candidate: New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to rule on whether these contracts are swaps or gambling, and a UK regulator weighed easing its ban on financial prediction markets.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Benjamin Netanyahu holds the premiership once Israel's next government is formed. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it turns on coalition arithmetic rather than on polling.
poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.recent: The Haaretz report that the UAE warned Netanyahu of a Hamas plan days before the 7 October attack surfaced this month, and he answered it with a threat of legal action. It landed as Smotrich pushed to claim Areas A and B outright and twelve states, France and the UK among them, moved to sanction settlement trade.

poly-will-no-fed-rate-cuts-happen-in-202.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged or higher for a full calendar year. It is a bet on the absence of easing, so it prices the risk that inflation keeps the central bank from cutting at all.
poly-will-no-fed-rate-cuts-happen-in-202.recent: An oil shock did the work: Houthis captured Yemen's port of Mocha, and a payroll surge pushed traders toward a September hike rather than a cut. Goldman Sachs abandoned its no-hike call, and the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5% ahead of the Fed meeting.

poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Bab el-Mandeb strait — the passage between Yemen and Djibouti joining the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden, and the southern gate of the Suez route — is shut to shipping. Priced in cents on the dollar.
poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.recent: Houthis captured Mocha, on Yemen's Red Sea coast, on 10 September, putting a port on the strait's approaches under the control of the party the contract is written about, and oil jumped on the news. Holding a harbour is not the same as closing a channel, and the contract has to resolve by the end of September.

poly-will-donald-trump-win-the-nobel-pea.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Norwegian Nobel Committee names Trump its Peace Prize laureate. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a forecast, and it tracks whether his diplomacy looks like something Oslo would reward.
poly-will-donald-trump-win-the-nobel-pea.recent: Trump said in Dublin the Iran war would end "very soon", then in Doonbeg tied that ending to the midterms — a peace on an electoral clock. He also ordered a halt to strikes on Russian diesel refineries, with US petrol at $4.27 a gallon and Brent near $109.50 a barrel.

poly-friedrich-merz-out-as-chancellor-of.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Friedrich Merz ceases to be Germany's chancellor before 2027. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it tracks the strain inside his governing coalition in Berlin.

poly-israel-x-lebanon-diplomatic-meeting.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Israel and Lebanon hold direct talks by a set date. Traders price the chance of negotiation between two states still exchanging fire across the Blue Line, so it moves on strikes and mediation, not on diplomacy alone.
poly-israel-x-lebanon-diplomatic-meeting.recent: Israeli artillery hit Zawtar al-Sharqiyah in the Nabatieh district on Sunday morning, days after a tunnel demolition at Ali al-Taher the US Geological Survey logged as a 4.1 tremor. The ridge overlooks Nabatieh and the Litani approaches, and holding it gives Israel terrain to bargain with rather than a reason to sit down.

poly-fed-rate-hike-by-october-2026-meeti.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve raises its policy rate at or before the October 2026 meeting. It trades as a price on an outcome, so it reprices on every inflation print and official remark that shifts the case for tightening.
poly-fed-rate-hike-by-october-2026-meeti.recent: A war premium did the repricing: Houthi fighters took Yemen's port of Mocha, oil ran to $105, and an oil shock argues for a hike rather than the cut the market had been carrying. Goldman Sachs dropped its no-hike call on Friday, and the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5% as traders positioned for the meeting.

poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-finis.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva places second in Brazil's presidential vote. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it is read as a gauge of how far the incumbent left has slipped.
poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-finis.recent: The only Brazilian item in the fortnight's feed was a corruption investigation opened into Flavio Bolsonaro as the election tightened, and that does not account for the repricing of where Lula places. Nothing else in the window bears on the race.

wiki-united-kingdom.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on the United Kingdom, a sovereign state of four nations governed from Westminster. Traffic on a country page rises when something puts that country in front of readers who do not normally follow it.
wiki-united-kingdom.recent: Trump said twice that Irish unification would be welcome, and reporting out of Doonbeg noted that a single UK official holds the power to call a border poll. Air traffic control failures stranded passengers across British airports, and the Commons rejected assisted dying after support collapsed by 45 votes since June.

stocks:AAPL.standing: The share price of Apple, the American maker of the iPhone, Mac and its own silicon, and one of the largest companies on the Nasdaq. Its hardware cycle pulls a supply chain across Asia along with it.
stocks:AAPL.recent: Apple launched the $1,999 iPhone Duo, a passport-shaped foldable, at a September event that had no standard iPhone 18 in it — a deliberate move upmarket — and shipped a rebuilt Siri in iOS 27 that reads a user's messages, photos and screen. John Ternus took over as chief executive from Tim Cook on 1 September.

stocks:GOOG.standing: The parent company of Google, YouTube and Android, listed on Nasdaq. Its revenue rests overwhelmingly on search advertising, so anything that changes where people type a question reaches this share price.
stocks:GOOG.recent: Apple shipped a rebuilt Siri in iOS 27 that reads a user's messages, photos and screen — the assistant layer on a billion phones, sitting between the user and whoever answers the query. Google's own releases stayed on the enterprise side, pricing a cybersecurity model per token out of Mountain View.

stocks:ORCL.standing: The database and enterprise-software company, now one of the largest sellers of rented cloud computing to companies training and running AI models. Its shares trade in New York, and its capital spending is a read on how fast that buildout is going.
stocks:ORCL.recent: Oracle told staff by email that the day they received it was their last, under a $700 million job-cut plan the company says funds data centres for AI. Larry Ellison scrapped a planned 50-million-share sale the day after the cuts were disclosed.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: A contract settling on whether Democrats win a majority of the 435 US House seats at the November 2026 midterms. Its price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it moves on candidate filings, polls and redistricting rulings.
poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's reporting bears on the race itself. What it carried instead was a challenge to the venue — New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to decide whether contracts like this one are swaps or gambling — and the argument that Trump's Iran war has become a midterm election problem.

poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Vladimir Putin ceases to be Russia's president before the end of 2026, by resignation, removal, incapacity or death. It is the cleanest traded read on how much regime risk sits behind every other Russia exposure.
poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.recent: Putin held the initiative through the window rather than losing it: he met Witkoff and Kushner in Moscow for three hours on a US push to end the war, then told an audience in New Delhi that European troops in Ukraine would make those countries parties to a war. At home the FSB ran a treason case against an embassy guard on a confession alone, and abroad Russia launched 863 drones at Ukraine in a single night and struck a Warsaw-bound train two kilometers from Poland.

poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-us-presi.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if JD Vance wins the 2028 US presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, read as a percentage, and it moves on the primary field and on the administration's standing.
poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-us-presi.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's political reporting touched Vance himself. What it carried was Trump's Iran war running into a midterm problem, and New Jersey asking the Supreme Court to decide whether prediction markets like this one may legally operate at all — a question about the venue, not about this contract.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Israel and Iran agree a ceasefire before the end of the year. Traders price it as a percentage, so the number is what a bet on peace costs rather than what any government has signalled.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: Talks the Gulf states were preparing to host in Muscat were shelved after a projectile killed a sailor off Qeshm Island, and Iran's Strait Authority began listing tanker insurers as non-compliant. Washington then denied Mohammad Eslami a visa for the IAEA conference in Vienna, closing one of the few venues where the two sides still meet.

poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-repub.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Senator Marco Rubio becomes the Republican Party's presidential nominee in 2028. It is one of the earliest liquid gauges of how a wide-open Republican primary field is being priced.
poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-repub.recent: The contract's own venue is under legal challenge: New Jersey has asked the Supreme Court to decide whether prediction markets trade regulated swaps or fall under state gambling law, and Britain's regulator is weighing whether to lift its ban on financial prediction markets. Nothing in the fortnight bears on Rubio himself.
